bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.locator: PDF page 7, printed page 736, Table 2, Wasatch front column
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.reference: Bjarnason & Pechmann (1989), BSSA 79(3), 731-755; model modified from model B of Keller et al. (1975)
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.role: GaMMA association eikonal + NonLinLoc absolute location for the 2020 Magna sequence
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.derivation: Wasatch front column of Table 2, transcribed verbatim. The 1989 modifications relative to Keller et al. (1975) model B were: (1) addition of a 7.9 km/s halfspace beginning at 42 km depth, and (2) increase of the depth of the top of the 7.5 km/s layer (to 28.0 km), distributed proportionately to all layers above for consistency with Loeb (1986) and Loeb & Pechmann (1986).
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.corroboration: Cited as the UUSS routine Wasatch front 1-D model by later UUSS work (e.g. Whidden et al. 2023, SRL; 2024 BSSA ML-arrival studies). This is the model family in routine UUSS use for the Salt Lake Valley where the 2020 Magna sequence lies.
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.vs_provenance: Derived as Vp / 1.73; the paper tabulates P-wave velocities only. Not an independently tabulated measurement.
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_wasatch_front.depth_reference: Table 2 footnote: 'Datum is 1500 m above sea level.' Layer-top depths are therefore below a 1.5 km ASL datum, which closely matches this case's association reference_elevation_km = 1.4 (mean station elevation ~1.48 km ASL); the residual 0.1 km datum offset is not corrected for and is noted here.

layer_semantics.published_representation: Depth to top of layer plus one constant P velocity per layer (standard layered model). Paper text: 'The P-wave velocity in our Wasatch front model is 5.9 km/sec over the depth range of 1.5 to 17.1 km'; near-source velocity estimated 5.9 +/- 0.2 km/s for most studied earthquakes.
layer_semantics.grid_use: Vel2Grid/NLLoc and the GaMMA eikonal treat these as layer tops with constant velocity per layer below the top, consistent with the Ridgecrest shelly_table1 convention in this repository.

bjarnason_pechmann_1989_plus_slv_basinfi.reference: Bjarnason & Pechmann (1989), BSSA 79(3), 731-755; model modified from model B of Keller et al. (1975)
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_plus_slv_basinfi.role: GaMMA association eikonal + NonLinLoc absolute location for the 2020 Magna sequence, round r4+
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_plus_slv_basinfi.derivation: BP89 Wasatch-front column with one structural addition: a low-velocity basin-fill layer, sea level to 2.0 km bsl (1.5-3.5 km below the model datum) at Vp 4.0 km/s, Vs = Vp/1.73. Motivation: BP89 puts 5.9 km/s immediately below sea level, a smoothed regional average that is too fast for the Salt Lake Valley sedimentary fill above the Magna sources; with BP89 the NLL catalog ran systematically late (median origin-time difference +0.34 s vs both pang and uuss) and the two non-basin levers (main-layer 5.9->5.7, Vp/Vs 1.73->1.68) both degraded depths without fixing dt. Selected by the r4 offline relocation sweep (2026-10-19, expert/PLAN.md): dt +0.34 -> +0.05 s (pang) / +0.04 s (uuss), depth/epicentral medians and matched counts unchanged or slightly improved, zero NLL failures.
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_plus_slv_basinfi.vs_provenance: Derived as Vp / 1.73; the paper tabulates P-wave velocities only. Not an independently tabulated measurement.
bjarnason_pechmann_1989_plus_slv_basinfi.depth_reference: Table 2 footnote: 'Datum is 1500 m above sea level.' Layer-top depths are therefore below a 1.5 km ASL datum, which closely matches this case's association reference_elevation_km = 1.4 (mean station elevation ~1.48 km ASL); the residual 0.1 km datum offset is not corrected for and is noted here.
